findings.namedBuyers: Emily Burns, Director, Education & Impact and 2027 OLA Staff Lead, is the primary conference-routing contact. Michelle Arbuckle, Executive Director, is the senior partnership/association contact. Meredith Tutching is the 2027 EXPO Lead and Director, Forest of Reading & Logistics on the planning-team page. Jennifer Marriott of Gap.Point.Reach Inc. is the show-management and room-rental/client-reception contact. All are commercially relevant routes; no public source identifies a named hotel-contract signatory.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming: January 27–30, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Official conference homepage gives the full activity dates; EXPO trading dates are January 28–29, not the entire conference. January 26 is a restricted exhibitor move-in date, not the conference opening. The discovery seed January 28 was incomplete. No official 2028 edition dates or venue were located; do not extrapolate dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel constraints and published event scale: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown fits a modest delegate, speaker, exhibitor-team or executive lodging allocation, not sole housing or the full conference venue. A proposed 15–109 peak-room allocation is a sales sizing scenario only, not published event demand, guaranteed inventory or a forecast. Harbourfront/downtown access to MTCC supports this city-conference role; no resort or extended-stay requirement was found. Historical 2026 scale was 4,153 in-person attendees; the prospectus separately reports 4,407 in-person plus virtual attendees. Neither is a 2027 forecast or a room count. Smaller side meetings are conceivable within supplied capacity, but existing programming is at MTCC/InterContinental. The hotel’s official site states “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; do not promise catered receptions or dining without operational confirmation.
findings.venueCommitments: Officially announced venue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, Hall C for EXPO, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6. Educational programmes also use the adjoining InterContinental Toronto Centre hotel. This is Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC territory, not an out-of-town resort. These are published venue commitments, not a newly open venue search; underlying contract terms were not published.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified editions: February 1–4, 2023; January 24–27, 2024; January 29–February 1, 2025; January 28–31, 2026. All were Toronto/MTCC-centred. The 2025 programme also identifies ICTC Ballroom activity. This researched timeline supports recurring Toronto demand, not a rotating-destination opportunity. It does not establish all historical host hotels or future contracts.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Direct OLA-negotiated conference blocks, booked via the official hotel links; no independently appointed housing bureau or open hotel RFP was identified. Source quote: “Each year, OLA negotiates discounted hotel rates for attendees at several hotels within walking distance of the conference venue.” Also: “OLA is responsible for attrition fees when hotel rooms are cancelled at the last minute”. Every hotel currently listed: InterContinental Toronto Centre; Delta Toronto Hotel; Toronto Marriott City Centre; Union Hotel (formerly Strathcona); Fairmont Royal York. InterContinental is labelled “Booking Link (Full)”; the other four have booking links, which do not prove live inventory. The InterContinental booking destination is explicitly titled “OLA 2027 Ontario Library Association”. The hotel page is a rolling page without a year in its heading; this 2027 booking destination and the 2027 conference context support edition attribution. No published block sizes, pickup, peak rooms, total room nights or specific cutoff date were found. OLA warns it is not working with external vendors to book hotel rooms; Passkey links are reservation technology, not proof of an independent housing bureau.
findings.organizationStructure: OLA is a non-profit library association and event owner, not a corporate relocation buyer or a DMC. Its staff lead educational programming and OLA expressly negotiates attendee hotel rates and bears attrition. Gap.Point.Reach Inc. is separately identified for show management and exhibitor/client-reception services; do not treat it as the attendee-housing buyer. Volunteer programme co-chairs are not evidenced as hotel buyers.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Five published incumbent hotel blocks already compete for the business. InterContinental has attached-venue convenience and is also a programme location. Its official block is marked full: evidence of that block status only, not proof that the entire hotel or destination is sold out, that other blocks are full, or that OLA needs another hotel. OLA’s disclosed attrition exposure makes displacement of existing blocks commercially sensitive. Radisson Blu is not listed as an official block hotel. No organizer-issued overflow request or quantified unmet demand was found.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Emily Burns at eburns@accessola.com and Michelle Arbuckle at marbuckle@accessola.com, using superconference@accessola.com as the general conference channel. Ask who owns hotel negotiations, whether any 2027 supplemental demand remains after incumbent pickup/attrition, and whether a small Harbourfront block would be considered. Only then propose a right-sized lodging offer with confirmed dates, inventory, rates, breakfast arrangements and terms; do not undercut or displace contracted blocks by assumption. If 2027 is closed, request a post-event review and the next hotel-block procurement timetable. Route exhibitor client-reception enquiries through Jennifer Marriott; verify hotel food/beverage operations before offering reception packages.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 dates and venue are accessible to research, but hotel sourcing is already allocated to published incumbent blocks. Radisson has no evidenced appointment, allocation or open RFP. Conditional access is limited to asking OLA whether an authorized supplemental block, speaker/exhibitor lodging or independently booked delegate option is wanted; do not call this sourcing open or assume demand from the full InterContinental block.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: pursue a modest future-cycle share of OLA’s recurring Toronto accommodation programme, rather than relocating the full conference. OLA states that hotel information is announced each August; request the next contracting/review timetable before that publication window, because contracting may be earlier. No 2028 edition dates, Toronto venue commitment or open sourcing mandate were verified. Future capture is a relationship strategy, not confirmed 2028 business.
